bibl.title: Siddhāntacandrikā
Vedāntasiddhāntacandrikā
bibl.note: A Descriptive Catalogue of the Sanskrit Manuscripts in the Sarasvati Mahal Library, Tanjore (Tanjore). Vols. 1–19.
Thiruvengadathan, A. Rāmabhadra Dīkṣita and His Works: A Study. Chennai: The Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, 2002.
Thangaswami, R. A Bibliographical Survey of Advaita Vedānta Literature. Madras: Rathnam Press, 1980.

A commentary on this work (Uddhāra/Udgāra) was written by Gaṅgādharendra Sarasvatī (1826) (see Dasgupta vol. 2, pg. 56 and R. Thangaswami, A Bibliographical Survey of Advaita Vedānta Literature pg. 387)

This work is complete in 50 verses. It asserts the Mīmāṃsā cannot lead to liberation, and that the Sāṅkhya, Yoga, and Nyāya śāstras are only doorkeepers to Advaita Vedānta (see R. Thangaswami, A Bibliographical Survey of Advaita Vedānta Literature pg. 387)

There are 51 verses, according to the Tanjore Descriptive Catalogue, A Descriptive Catalogue of the Sanskrit Manuscripts in the Sarasvati Mahal Library, Tanjore (Tanjore). Vols. 1–19: vol. 13, p. 5817–5819, ms. 7694.
Ms. 7695 in the volume above is a commentary on this work called the Siddhāntacandrikāvyākhyā Udgāraḥ.
